transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Doctor. Well, I'm here because I just can't seem to turn off my worrying once it starts. It's frustrating because I'll tell myself that I've already made the list, checked the dates, and done everything I reasonably can to prepare for whatever it is... but my mind just won't stop. I just can't seem to shut it off.
How long have you been experiencing this constant, hard-to-control worrying—has it been going on for six months or more, or did it start more recently after a specific event?

It's been going on for about seven months now. It started... well, shortly after a friend of mine passed away. We had some projects we were working on together, and I tried to keep them moving forward on my own, and that's really when all this constant worrying began.

Is your worrying mostly focused on things connected to your friend's passing and the projects you took over, or do you also find yourself worrying a lot about other things in your life—like your health, finances, family, or work—that aren't related to that at all?

It's really not just the projects anymore. My mind just keeps roaming all over the place. I'll start out thinking about the exhibition schedule, and then... well, suddenly I'm worrying about my daughter's travel plans, or whether the house gutters need fixing. It just spreads to everything. It's like these small things start to feel as if they could just unravel into something much bigger.
Along with the worrying, have you noticed physical or mental symptoms like feeling restless or on edge, tiring easily, muscle tension, trouble sleeping, or difficulty concentrating?

Well, I've definitely noticed the tiring easily part. Even when I actually manage to sleep through the night, I wake up feeling as if I have already put in half a day's work. It's very draining. By the time I do something simple around the house, like water the garden beds or sort out some papers for my book club, I just... I need to sit down and gather myself. I just seem to run out of energy so quickly lately.
Have you been having trouble concentrating or find your mind going blank lately, like when reading, having a conversation, or focusing on tasks?

No, I haven't really noticed any problems with my concentration. I can still read my books and keep up with conversations just fine. My mind doesn't go blank or anything like that. It's really just the worrying and the tiredness that are bothering me.
Have you noticed feeling unusually restless, keyed up, or on edge, or experiencing muscle tension or aches, along with the worrying?

Yes, I definitely feel that on edge feeling. I often feel wound up even just sitting in my own living room. I'll find myself tapping my fingers when I'm on a phone call, or I just have to get up and straighten something on a shelf. Sitting quietly just makes me feel jumpy lately.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with excessive, difficult-to-control worry spanning multiple life domains (work projects, family travel, household matters) for approximately 7 months, exceeding the 6-month threshold for GAD. Associated symptoms include being easily fatigued, restlessness/feeling on edge/keyed up, and subjective muscle tension/fidgeting (finger tapping, need to straighten objects). Although onset followed a bereavement, the worry has generalized well beyond grief-related themes to unrelated topics, and the symptom profile (multiple associated somatic/psychic symptoms, chronicity, pervasive uncontrollable worry) is more consistent with GAD than an adjustment disorder tied specifically to the loss. Concentration difficulties and sleep disturbance were explicitly denied, but the diagnostic threshold (3+ associated symptoms) is still met via fatigue and restlessness/muscle tension equivalents. No mood elevation, panic attacks, or psychotic features reported, ruling out other primary anxiety or mood disorders.
